one_line: Warrior queen of Garha-Katanga (Gondwana) who resisted Mughal expansion under Akbar.

appearance.age_look: early 30s, athletic and battle-hardened yet regal
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes with thick lashes, a small beauty mark near the left cheek, and a calm but resolute default expression that hardens with quiet determination.
appearance.hair: Long, straight black hair parted in the middle, oiled and drawn back into a single thick braid reaching mid-back, wrapped at the base with a narrow red cloth band; she wears a simple gold maang-tikka at the parting and small gold hoop earrings, plus a narrow gold circlet barely visible beneath her braid wrap.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate mid-16th-century central Indian royal-warrior attire: a deep-red quilted cotton choli-blouse fully covering the torso and upper arms, over which she wears a fitted, sleeved, knee-length padded cotton angarkha coat in muted marigold yellow with subtle block-printed floral motifs in darker ochre; below, a full, ankle-length dark green ghagra-style skirt with wide flare, worn over cotton trousers for riding; a rich indigo-blue odhani/dupatta with a thin gold border drapes securely from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back, firmly covering the bodice; she has a wide brown leather belt at the waist with a simple brass buckle and a small attached pouch; jewellery is restrained but royal—two slim gold bangles on each wrist and a single string of small gold beads at the neck; footwear is brown leather 16th-century-style mojari shoes with upturned toes, practical for riding and marching.
appearance.signature: A medium-length curved talwar sword with a plain steel blade, a slightly flared disc pommel, and a simple brass hilt wrapped in dark brown leather, worn at her left hip in a brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings.

ref_desc: Rani Durgavati is a medium-brown, sharp-eyed woman in her early 30s with a long black braid, deep-red padded blouse, marigold angarkha coat, dark green ghagra, indigo dupatta, brown leather belt, modest gold jewellery, and a brass-hilted talwar at her left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Rani Durgavati as a 16th-century central Indian warrior queen: an athletic woman in her early 30s with a warm medium-brown complexion, oval face, sharp dark eyes and a small beauty mark near her left cheek, wearing her straight black hair parted in the middle and gathered into a single thick braid to mid-back held with a narrow red cloth band, a simple gold maang-tikka at the hair parting, small gold hoop earrings and a slim gold circlet mostly hidden by her braid wrap; dress her in a deep-red quilted cotton blouse that fully covers her torso and upper arms, over which sits a fitted knee-length padded angarkha coat in muted marigold yellow decorated with subtle darker-ochre floral block prints, and a full ankle-length dark green ghagra skirt over hidden trousers suited for riding; drape a rich indigo-blue dupatta with a thin gold border from her left shoulder diagonally across her chest and around her back so the bodice remains modestly covered; cinch her waist with a brown leather belt holding a small pouch, add minimal royal jewellery with two slim gold bangles on each wrist and a single strand of small gold beads at the neck, and put her in brown leather mojari shoes with slightly upturned toes; at her left hip hang a medium-length curved talwar sword with a plain steel blade and brass hilt wrapped in dark brown leather, sheathed in a brown leather scabbard with simple brass fittings; keep colours rich and matte (deep red, marigold, dark green, indigo, brown leather) and pose her front, side and back with a calm but resolute expression suited for the Mughal-era Narrai and Chauragarh campaigns.
